image_description: A close-up, high-resolution shot of the head and upper jaw of a Nile crocodile. The image focuses on the textured, armored skin (scutes) around the eye and snout. The eye is visible with a vertical slit pupil. Several large, conical teeth are visible along the jawline, including the characteristic fourth tooth of the lower jaw fitting into a notch in the upper jaw. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing cracks and rough osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout tapers to a point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears broad and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple conical teeth are clearly visible along the jawline. They appear interlocked and substantial, matching the description of massive jaws.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on the top surface of the head (dorsal). The pupil is clearly a vertical slit. The nictitating membrane is not clearly deployed but the eye structure is anatomically correct for a crocodilian.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tip of the snout is cut off by the frame; nostrils are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the full body isn't visible, the visible neck and head transition show heavy armor plating (osteoderms) consistent with an elongated, armored body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture shows distinct, raised, bony plates (scutes) with a rough appearance. While 'longitudinal rows' are hard to verify in a tight crop, the presence of scutes is undeniable.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of grey, tan, and brown earth tones. The texture is visibly rough and cracked, matching the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the dorsal/lateral side of the head and jaw. The ventral surface (belly) is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs or feet are visible in this close-up crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Nile Crocodile vs other crocodilians) based on fine-grained features like snout shape and tooth arrangement.
To analyze the complex texture of the scutes for any signs of AI-generated smoothing, repetition patterns, or unnatural blending.
To ensure the teeth are distinct entities properly embedded in the jaw and not melting into the gums or each other, a common AI artifact in close-ups.

focus_areas: Anatomical correctness of the eye and pupil
Integration of teeth into the jawbone
Lighting and shadow consistency on the rough skin
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the boundary between the teeth and the gum line. AI often struggles with the precise occlusion and embedding of individual teeth in realistic close-ups. Also, verify if the skin texture exhibits any 'tiling' or repetitive patterns indicative of generative models.
